overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data highlights a clear viewer preference for extreme 'What If' space scenarios and exotic planetary phenomena over general psychology or biology shorts. Videos leveraging hypothetical immersion ('What If You Fell Into...') and rare planetary anomalies (diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) consistently achieve the highest views-per-day and engagement ratios (likes-per-view). Conversely, standard biological facts and psychological tricks display lower velocity. Growth should double down on immersive astronomical what-if scenarios with visual spectacle.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) pull over 900-1000+ views rapidly with strong like counts (38 and 18 likes respectively), outperforming standard declarative facts.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize high-concept 'What If' cosmic survival questions that force the viewer to imagine physical interaction with extreme environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: Exotic Planetary Anomalies with Extreme Extremes
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible weather or materials on distant worlds—such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0)—achieve top-tier view velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future scripts on newly discovered or lesser-known exoplanets featuring bizarre physics, extreme temperatures, or bizarre meteorological events.

weak_patterns.pattern: General Psychology and Brain Trick Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5AN7LUgqarc, 2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) stall out with very low views (<70) and minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone human psychology facts and cognitive tricks unless framed within a high-stakes survival or sci-fi context.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated basic animal facts (e.g., octopus hearts, eternal life animals) plateau quickly after initial publishing without attracting high comment or like ratios.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard listicle-style animal facts unless transformed into cinematic animal survival micro-narratives.
